standard_prerequisites.name: Cohomology of a sheaf of modules computed from an injective resolution
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard in this chapter: H^n(U, F) is the n-th cohomology of the complex of sections of an injective resolution F -> I^bullet
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the displayed presentation of H^n(U, F) and the representative chosen in the proof; the covering argument is the counted content.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exactness of the resolution in positive degrees
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard sheaf theory: for n > 0 the image sheaf of d equals the kernel sheaf, so a section of the kernel over U becomes a coboundary after restriction to a covering
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the local primitives xi_i; identifying them and concluding the vanishing of the restricted class is inside the counted proof.

core_obligations: Present the class: take an injective resolution F -> I^bullet and use the displayed description of H^n(U, F) as the kernel of I^n(U) -> I^{n+1}(U) modulo the image of I^{n-1}(U) -> I^n(U) to choose a representative tilde xi in I^n(U) of the given class xi (proof lines 570-577).

Find local primitives: since n > 0 the resolution is exact in degree n, so the image sheaf of the differential equals the kernel sheaf; as tilde xi is a section of the kernel sheaf over U, there is an open covering U = union U_i with tilde xi|_{U_i} in the image of d from I^{n-1}(U_i) (proof lines 578-586).
Conclude: by the definition of the restriction of a cohomology class as the class of the restricted representative, each xi|_{U_i} vanishes, which is the assertion (proof lines 586-588).
proof_roadmap: Write the cohomology group as a quotient of sections of an injective resolution and pick a representative of the class (proof lines 570-577).
Use exactness in degree n to make the representative locally a coboundary over an open covering (proof lines 578-585).
Translate back through the definition of restriction to get xi|_{U_i} = 0 for all i (proof lines 586-588).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a ringed space X, a sheaf of O_X-modules F, an open subspace U and a class xi in H^n(U, F) with n > 0, there is an open covering of U over which xi restricts to zero (statement lines 560-566). The argument is the two-step use of an injective resolution: first the class is presented as a quotient of sections of I^n(U) and a representative is chosen, and then exactness of the resolution in degree n is used to know that the representative is locally a coboundary, which is what produces the covering (proof lines 570-586). The conclusion is immediate once one remembers that restriction of a class is computed on representatives. The claim is H2: no construction of its own, but two genuinely different uses of the same resolution.
